question: Which process is sometimes called "reduction division" because it reduces the number of chromosomes to half the normal number to form sperm and eggs?
solution:
The correct answer is __Meiosis__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Meiosis is a type of cell division in which a single cell divides two times to produce 4 daughter cells.
 
• Meiosis is also called reductional division as the number of chromosomes gets reduced to half after the process.
 
• Meiosis occurs in sex cells and results in the formation of Haploid Gametes__ (cell that contains a single set of chromosomes).
 
• 1 male sex cell divides meiotically to produce 4 male gametes, and all of them are functional.
 
• Whereas 1 female sex cell divides meiotically to produce 4 female gametes (eggs).
 
 
• ​In plants 3 of these gametes degenerate and only one remains functional.
 
 
 
• Zygote is formed by the fusion of male and female gametes, this process is known as Syngamy.
